notes: A machine that reconnects no longer loses its UDP port forward. Reported from a live router: when the build server drops off and comes back, its RustDesk NAT port stops working until you wait a while or open the NAT table and save it again. Both halves were the clue -- waiting is RustDesk falling back to its slower TCP relay, saving again is the only path that carries the missing fields. enabled/comments/udp exist only in the request body, so a client loaded from the database carries three empty strings, and ReconcileNATPorts rebuilt every nat_ports row from them. A guard for exactly this already existed and its comment already described the failure; it just asked whether the caller PASSED the arguments rather than whether the values were there, and ReconcileClientUpdate always passes all three. The DHCP sweep calls that path whenever an address changes, which is what a reconnect does. Also: a changed admin password now survives a reboot -- chpasswd writes /etc/shadow, which on this router is part of the RAM overlay, so the new password worked until the next boot and then silently reverted to the one baked into the ISO; the hash is now kept on the persist partition and restored on boot, and it is deliberately not writable through the settings API. And brand mode: a captive advertisement page like restaurant wifi, with image or video, seasonal canvas effects (Tet, Mid-autumn, Christmas, rain, leaves, heat, or automatic by date), optional date-of-birth/phone/confirmation-code collection, expiry with a one-minute grace so a brief wifi drop does not send a guest back to the advert, and a Brand tab to set it all up. Plus a Notes section on the Info tab, a DHCP pool starting at 20.20.200.1 with a migration for existing routers and an ARP-sweep cap so the wider pool cannot revive the v0.4.93 broadcast storm, and tests that fail the build when a UI string or placeholder exists in only one language.
